decision: Which mix of A (book path) and B (grade climb) should show where the child can go, and in which visual language?
evidence: Savar, 2026-11-11, after round r-progress-preview: 'I like a mix of A and B ... I'm not happy with the visuals just yet.' No build yet.
primary_axis: visual language of the A+B mix (precise chart, product cover, dark poster, illustration)
invariants: same three cases, pace model, headline and basis line as round 1 (pace.js, levels.js unchanged)
every option shows both the books (A) and the climb over time to the goal (B)
books drawn in the workbook cover's language: white paper, 3x3 colour grid, yellow highlight (public/whats-included/wb/leah-01-cover.jpg)
no level ids shown to a parent; grades label groups of books (D-218)

options.bet: A staircase chart: each grade a step, books stand on it, months across, flag on top
options.benefit: Most honest picture: progress happens a grade at a time; every book is visible; clean and light
options.risk: Reads as an analytics graph, not a child's plan

options.bet: Lead with a real-looking Book 1 cover made for the child, beside the climb line of book dots
options.benefit: The product is the picture: 'made for Leah'; tapping a dot shows any book's cover and topic
options.cost: The cover takes a lot of space on a phone
options.risk: The line is thin next to the cover; the goal is less loud

options.bet: A dark poster: 'Grade 1 -> Grade 3' in big type, each book a spine that rises with the grade, flag at the end
options.benefit: The strongest single image; best as the email still and a screenshot a parent shares
options.cost: Dark block differs from the light report
options.risk: Rising bars can read as scores, not books

options.bet: An illustrated trail up a hill: books as stepping stones, grade signposts, a flag on the top
options.benefit: The warmest and most child-like; a journey, not a chart
options.cost: Most custom drawing to build and keep right for every case
options.risk: Can feel childish to a parent; the dates are less exact to read

recommendation: G for the report and the email still, with F's tap-a-book cover as the detail; or E if Savar wants the lighter report look
